title: Fail-safe: adaptive rollback heuristics for canary/A-B rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal:
Implement an automated rollback subsystem for model rollout pipelines (canary, A/B, and shadow traffic) that decides safe failure actions based on multi-dimensional SLO signals: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token cost per request, and throughput (requests/sec and concurrency). The subsystem must be tunable per-project and exposed in the Console for rollout configuration and post-mortem analysis.

Scope:
- Controller lives in rollout service and evaluates rollouts every evaluation_window (default 1m) using a sliding window (default 5m/15m for two tiers).
- Metrics: p95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx classification), token cost per 1k tokens, throughput (rps), and synthetic quality guardrails (when available from eval metrics).
- Triggers: multi-metric scoring plus hard thresholds. Two independent paths: (1) hard absolute thresholds (eg. error_rate > 5% for 3 consecutive windows) and (2) aggregated risk score that combines z-scores of normalized metric deltas vs baseline.
- Safety: require minimum sample size (default 200 requests to canary) before any auto-rollback. Implement cooldown windows (default 10m) after a rollback to prevent flip-flopping. Manual overrides and forced rollbacks must be respected.

Design highlights / heuristics:
1) Baseline & dynamic thresholds:
   - Compute baseline from the last N days of production traffic for the target model variant (default N=7). Use median and MAD to capture variance rather than mean+std to be robust to spikes. Dynamic thresholds set at baseline + k*MAD (k configurable), with conservative defaults (k=3 for latency, k=5 for token cost to avoid noisy cost fluctuations).
2) Aggregated risk score:
   - Normalize each metric delta by its MAD -> z-like score. Weight metrics (default weights: error_rate=0.45, p95_latency=0.35, throughput=0.15, token_cost=0.05). RiskScore = sum(weight * clipped_normalized_delta). If RiskScore > 1.0 for M consecutive windows (configurable M=2) trigger rollback.
3) Hard fail cases:
   - Error rate absolute threshold: if error_rate increases by >3 percentage points AND absolute error_rate > 2% for two consecutive windows, immediate rollback.
   - Throughput collapse: if observed throughput drops by >40% vs baseline for 2 consecutive windows, immediate rollback.
   - Token cost runaway: if cost per 1k tokens increases >50% and correlates with latency or error spikes, mark for rollback (and flag for manual review if sample size low).
4) Statistical tests & sample size:
   - Use two-sample proportion z-test for error rates (with continuity correction) and bootstrap medians for latency when sample sizes permit. Enforce min_sample_size=200 for any automated action; if below, generate alert but do not auto-rollback unless a hard fail applies.
5) Canary/A-B specifics:
   - Canary: progressive ramping with automated evaluation at each step. If rollback triggered at a ramp step, revert traffic to previous stable variant and mark canary as failed.
   - A/B tests: support per-variant thresholds and aggregate experiment-level checks to avoid noisy per-variant flips.
   - Shadow: metrics from shadow traffic cannot cause rollback but will surface to risk scoring dashboard; recommend manual rollout when shadow metrics look healthy for 24h.

Operational behavior & integrations:
- Rollout controller calls rollout-telemetry to fetch aggregated metrics from Observability (Console metrics API).
- Create an event in the audit log for any automatic rollback with reason, evaluation windows, and contributing metrics (for compliance).
- Wire automatic PagerDuty alert + Slack channel post when rollback occurs, including a one-click link to the runbook and responsible on-call.
- Console: add a rollback configuration panel per rollout (enable/disable auto-rollback, edit thresholds, weights, min sample size, cooldown). Provide a playback of the last 3 windows and the risk-score time series.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simplicity vs sensitivity: default conservative thresholds to avoid false positives; provide power-user knobs for product teams who prefer aggressive rollback behavior.
- Statistical rigor vs operational speed: bootstrap tests are slower; use approximate z-scores for sub-minute decisions with a secondary check (bootstrap) before irreversible actions where sample size allows.
- Cost automation: auto-rollback for token cost increases is gated by correlation with latency/errors to avoid rolling back for benign cost drift.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field) and rollout plan:
- Implementation should be feature-flagged and disabled by default in prod; enable for internal dogfood environment first. Run canary simulations with traffic replay (traffic-replay job id referenced below).

Additional notes:
- Requires small telemetry schema change: rollout event must carry per-variant sample counts and aggregated token counts per window. Coordinate with Observability team (ENG-4721).
- UX mockups linked in links field.
acceptance_criteria: Automated rollback executes in the sandbox when synthetic traffic triggers the defined hard-fail conditions (test harness: traffic-replay/2026-03-08).
RiskScore-based rollback fires after 2 consecutive evaluation windows in a simulated burst test with >200 sample size and observability shows contributing metric weights.
Console exposes per-rollout auto-rollback toggle and editable thresholds; UI changes pass design review and usability test with Solutions team.
Audit log entries are created for each auto-rollback with metric snapshots and are queryable by rollout_id.
PagerDuty/Slack integration notifies on-call with rollback reason and runbook link for at least 90% of rollbacks during the internal pilot.
Unit and e2e tests cover both canary and A/B rollback paths and enforce min_sample_size behavior.
Security/compliance checklist completed for storing metric snapshots in the audit trail (ENG-Sec review sign-off).
